change: No change. Primary obliques (both heads) and secondary abs + Quads/Rectus Femoris are correct. Rectus Femoris is valid for the knee-raise hip flexion component. EMG and biomechanics sources confirm obliques as prime mover, abs and hip flexors as secondary.

No change. Chest (both heads) as primary and Anterior Deltoids as secondary is correct for the wall pec stretch. The anterior deltoid and pectorals are co-stretched during this movement. trackingMode=timed is appropriate for a static stretch.

No change. Primary Anterior Deltoids is correct for the alternating overhead arm raise pattern. Secondary chest/Clavicular Head and mid back/Upper Traps are appropriate — upper traps assist in arm elevation and chest/clavicular head is lightly stretched as the arm moves overhead. trackingMode=repsOnly is correct for the alternating dynamic movement.

Changed secondary from Abductor->Abductor to glutes->Gluteus Medius. The Gluteus Medius is the primary hip stabilizer during single-leg balance (confirmed by multiple sources), making it more accurate than the generic Abductor/tensor for the stabilizing role in this stretch.

Changed secondary from Abductor->Abductor to glutes->Gluteus Medius, same rationale as standing_quadriceps_stretch. The side-angle variant is biomechanically identical for muscle involvement; Gluteus Medius is the key hip stabilizer during the single-leg balance position.
